purpose: Every place this estate records work that is not finished, declared in one file so that npm run outstanding can total them. Until 2026-09-14 there were five such places and no command that knew about more than two: npm run readiness counted 48 items, npm run commission counted those plus the governance findings, and the other three were counted by nothing. A question as ordinary as 'how much is left' had no answer, and each source read as if it were the whole picture.
whyFederatedRatherThanMerged: Merging them was the obvious move and it is the wrong one. The governance findings gate no pilot key, so folding them into a register whose every other row does would misrepresent both. The two audits are records — this estate does not rewrite a record to make it a task list, for the same reason docs/audits/ is exempt from every claim gate. And the pending-work register belongs to a workstream with its own owner. What was missing was never one register; it was one TOTAL. A source may keep its own shape, its own lifecycle and its own owner, and still be counted. Revised 2026-10-02: the pending-work register and the 2026-09-09 notification assessment were folded into the readiness register after both proved to be a second and third place holding the same notification work, with no way to close an entry in either. See 'retired'.
howToAddOne: Add an entry here. tests/outstanding-sources.test.mjs fails when a register-shaped document exists under docs/ and is not declared, so a new register cannot quietly become a sixth place nobody counts.

sources.title: Production readiness register
sources.authority: The register of record for commissioning. PLAN.md and closure-disposition.json are generated from it; npm run test:closure holds every document and npm run commission itself to it. Until 2026-09-24 the generated set was ACTION_PLAN.md, EXECUTION_RUNBOOK.md and IMPLEMENTATION_WALKTHROUGH.md, which PLAN.md replaced.

sources.title: Governance estate position
sources.authority: The ten SharePoint lists that carry identity, RBAC and audit. Kept separate because the endpoint commissioning path does not touch them today — but the seven internal designer-paste packages that will serve the pilot keys all read DGO_UserDirectory and DGO_RoleCatalogue, so that separation is a fact about the currently deployed flows, not a permanent property.

sources.title: Flow-truth persistence review
sources.allOpenBecause: A record is not edited to agree with the present, so no finding is ever closed in place. Until 2026-09-15 that meant all 29 stayed counted open: the rebuilt DGO_FLOW_TRUTH_PERSISTENCE package answered most of them, but tests/flow-truth-persistence.test.mjs asserted no finding by id, so nothing established WHICH. Something does now — see supersededBy. The default is still open; a finding leaves it only when the declaration names the assertion that answers it.

supersededBy.because: The rebuilt package is held to this finding by a named assertion in tests/flow-truth-persistence.test.mjs, which fails if the defect returns.
supersededBy.note: This supersedes the PACKAGE defect each finding raises. It resolves nothing in the tenant: B1's three lists still do not exist, and the assertion that covers B1 is precisely that the package says so rather than pretending otherwise. tests/flow-truth-coverage.test.mjs holds the declaration to both documents it spans — every finding in the review is declared, and every assertion cited exists in the suite.

whyUncountedSourcesAreStillDeclared: A document can be register-shaped and still not be a place work hides — because it RESTATES a counted source, or because it is a record whose live findings have since been taken up elsewhere. Those are declared here with counted:false and the reason, rather than left out. Leaving them out would mean the declaration could not be checked against the repository, and a silent exemption list is how a sixth register eventually appears: somebody adds a file, the gate is quiet, and nobody ever decides. Declared-and-uncounted is a decision on the record. npm run outstanding prints them so the judgement can be disagreed with.

retiredSources.rule: A declared source whose document is deleted is removed from `sources` and recorded here, with the document it was and where its subject went. It is not repointed at a surviving document: two declarations naming one path are two claims that one document is two sources, and the totals would double-count it the moment either became countable.
retiredSources.why: The thirty-six deployment documents became six. Every entry below was declared as register-shaped and deliberately not counted, so removing it changes no total — it removes a declaration about a document that no longer exists.
